title: Wall St Week Ahead As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings
key_facts: Reuters, 16 Oct: AI-linked shares, including chip and hardware firms such as Dell, struggled this week; results due next week from Meta, Lam Research, Texas Instruments, SpaceX and Tesla will test confidence in the rally.
CoreWeave, an AI cloud company with about $50 billion of debt, tumbled this week; Deutsche Bank and RBC strategists pulled back on tech recommendations.
The S&P 500 was only about 2% below its record high set this month; healthcare and consumer staples gained on the week.
S&P 500 companies are expected to raise third-quarter earnings by more than 30% (LSEG IBES).
Five AI hyperscalers are expected to raise combined capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year (Goldman Sachs).
The Philadelphia semiconductor index is down about 12% this month but up 57% on the year.
Hot inflation data boosted bets on a Fed rate rise at the end of October; most investors still expect the Fed to wait until December.
quote_evidence: Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms.
Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs.

"One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth.
why_it_matters_hint: Next week's company results will show whether AI spending is turning into profit.
notes: Forward-looking Reuters Week Ahead column, read on the Devdiscourse copy (reuters.com page returned 401). The S&P 500 weekly-loss comparison differs between this piece (biggest since June) and the Reuters market wrap (steepest since January); it is not used here.
